subject.title: Require explicit Keychain interaction for Chromium cookies

question: Should Chromium imports preserve the released interactive-retry default with an explicit non-interactive scope, or intentionally become fail-closed by default and require every host to opt in?
rationale: The patch changes a released credential-access and import-success contract, and source inspection cannot determine whether compatibility or secure background behavior is the repository's intended default.

options.title: Preserve compatibility
options.body: Keep interactive recovery as the default, add an explicit host-scoped non-interactive policy, and bound any permitted import to one interactive attempt.

options.title: Approve breaking default
options.body: Adopt explicit opt-in as the default only with a deliberate breaking-release plan, migration documentation, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep interactive recovery as the default, add an explicit host-scoped non-interactive policy, and bound any permitted import to one interactive attempt.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner released the current Chromium Keychain behavior and is best positioned to choose its compatibility contract.
